text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- No new legislation needed to improve quality of corporate
governance, says special committee of Amsterdam Stock Exchange.
- Chemicals concern DSM's Q3 net pressured by high oil
price. (p1)
- Investment fund NEBM plans to re-submit 1995 accounts for
approval at today's shareholders meeting. (p1)
- Rotterdam-based container transhipment firm ECT considers chance small that Amsterdam-based U.S. Ceres will become
fearsome rival. (p13)
- Papermaker KNP BT unit BT Office Products takes over
Kuipers of Zwolle. (p3)
- Philips Electronics subsidiary Taiwan Semiconductor
Manufacturing Co. books 22.6 pct higher Q3 net. (p4)
- Publisher Wegener's unit Suurland Falkplan to take over
Jong Holland of Apeldoorn. (p3)
- Builder HBG's Irish subsidiary Ascon gets orders for roads
around Dublin. (p3)
VOLKSKRANT
- Job guarantee for Fokker is stumbling block in takeover negotiations with Samsung. (p1)
- Parliament votes down cabinet's plans for increasing
tobacco excise. (p1)
- Strikes almost certain after unions and Dutch Railways
break off pay and conditions talks. (p3)
- Growing number of businesses want to change from PTT
Telecom to another company, according to accountants Moret,
Ernst & Young research. (p19)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Rediscovering your stolen car now profitable after High Court rules insurers must pay finder's reward. (p1)
- Threatening crisis forces cabinet to postpone decision on Maastricht Airport's night flight regime. (p3)
- Share price of entertainment group Endemol rises to Dfl 54 in "grey circuit" after subscriptions close yesterday. (p23)
- Cut-price airline EasyJet promises to stop advertisment
describing travel agents as "unnecessary and expensive frill".
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Dutch model for sound economy finds wide approval in
surrounding countries. (p1)
- Web surfing costs many working hours. (p1)
TROUW
- Freddy Heineken's biographer Barbara Smit says at
presentation that brewer threatened to prevent publication. (p1)
